invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.
Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works.
Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too.
Appearance is proved by screenshot tests in the tests repo, accessible names, or GOV.UK values read at run time, never by fixed colour, size or class assertions (Sam, 23 Oct engineering review).
A user's own input error shown back on the form is not logged (.claude/rules/code-quality.md, Logging and errors).
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Identification details: pressing Enter in a card for several animals keeps what the trader typed
increments.detail: Pressing Enter in a field on a card for several animals fires the page's hidden 'finish' button, which reads only one-animal cards, so the trader lands on the overview and what they typed is dropped with no message. Before the snagging build, Enter saved the half-filled entry. Waits on Sam's decision: make Enter save the card being typed in (or keep the trader on the page), or accept the drop and say so in the spec. A unit test currently pins the drop as a 'safe default' (animal-identification.controller.test.js:683-705).
acceptanceCriteria: Given a card for several animals with a value typed into one of its fields, when the trader presses Enter, then what happens matches Sam's decision, and the behaviour is written as a scenario in live-animals/journey-pages/identification-details spec.md. (review:engineering-2026-10-23 identification, medium)
The same holds without JavaScript. (invariant)
The unit test that pins the current drop is replaced by one that proves the decided behaviour. (review:engineering-2026-10-23)
